c.tagline: Sugar-town-turned-resort gateway to Saona, golf, and a Mediterranean village.

taxi.fareNote: Uber operates but coverage is limited outside the resorts; most taxis are unmetered, so agree the fare before you get in. Motoconcho scooter-taxis are the cheapest way around town.

emergency.note: 911 is the national emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the Dominican Republic.

hood_landmark.La Romana Centro: Parque Central La Romana Dominican Republic
hood_landmark.Casa de Campo: Casa de Campo Resort La Romana golf
hood_landmark.Casa de Campo Marina: Casa de Campo Marina La Romana
hood_landmark.Bayahíbe: Bayahibe fishing village beach Dominican Republic

avoid.reason: No formal no-go zones, but skip the low-income barrios away from the Marina, Casa de Campo and central tourist areas after dark due to street crime.
Motorbike bag-snatching and pickpocketing occur downtown and around the public market; keep phones out of sight.

hood_desc: The working heart of the city around the Parque Central and Mercado Modelo, with local eateries, shops, and the cruise port; the most authentic, walkable base and the cheapest place to stay.

A private, gated 7,000-acre resort community next to the city with three championship golf courses (Teeth of the Dog is rated the Caribbean's best), a marina, equestrian center, private beaches, and the Altos de Chavón artisan village; best for a self-contained luxury stay.
The stylish yacht harbor within Casa de Campo, designed to feel like an Italian fishing village, lined with waterfront restaurants, designer boutiques, and bars; the area's dining-and-nightlife hub.

A laid-back fishing village east of the city and the launch point for boats to Isla Saona and Isla Catalina and the gateway to Parque Nacional del Este; a mix of local color, dive shops, and small hotels.
The beach-resort strip just south of Bayahíbe fronting the long white-sand Playa Dominicus, packed with all-inclusive resorts; a relaxed, family-friendly base for sun and diving.

water.note: Drink bottled water; tap water is not considered safe for visitors.

transit.hours: Guaguas and city públicos run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; motoconchos and taxis fill late-night gaps.
transit.note: La Romana has no metro, tram, or rail; getting around means shared guaguas/públicos (minivans and cars on fixed routes), motoconcho scooter-taxis, and regular taxis.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver (públicos around 20-30 pesos, motoconchos a bit more); there is no rechargeable transit card.

bus: Express coaches to Santo Domingo, Higüey & Punta Cana (Expreso Bávaro, SITRABAPU)
ferry: Cruise terminal at Casa de Campo
Day-trip boats from Bayahíbe to Isla Saona & Isla Catalina

transit.m: Taxi to La Romana / Casa de Campo (10-15 min)
Guagua/públicos from the main road into town (cash, ~20 min)

tip.r: Restaurants add a 10% 'ley' service charge plus 18% tax; leaving another 5-10% for good service is customary.
